question: Suppose the Bayesian Network (BN) model for total recovery time initially assumes a lognormal prior with median 30 days and logarithmic standard deviation 0.5. posterior_log_std = 0.3  # dimensionless (log scale)

# 90% credible interval: 5th and 95th percentiles
# For lognormal, percentile p: exp(mu + z * sigma), where mu = ln(median), sigma = log_std
# z for 5th percentile = -1.6448536269514722 (approx -1.645)
# z for 95th percentile = 1.6448536269514722 (approx 1.645)

# Prior 90% credible interval
prior_mu = log(prior_median_days)  # natural log of median

prior_upper = exp(prior_mu + z_90 * prior_log_std)  # days

# Width of credible intervals

# a(t) = a_0 * sin(2*pi*t/T)
# Sliding occurs when a_0 * sin(2*pi*t/T) > a_y (assuming positive direction)
# sin(2*pi*t/T) > a_y/a_0 = 0.2/0.4 = 0.5

# t > T * (pi/6) / (2*pi) = T/12

t_start = T * asin(a_y / a_0) / (2 * pi)  # s

# End of sliding (by symmetry of sine wave)
t_end = T - t_start  # s

# During sliding, relative acceleration = a(t) - a_y
# a_rel(t) = a_0 * sin(2*pi*t/T) - a_y

# Velocity at end of sliding: integral of a_rel from t_start to t_end
# v = ∫[t_start to t_end] (a_0 * sin(2*pi*t/T) - a_y) dt
# = [-a_0 * T/(2*pi) * cos(2*pi*t/T) - a_y * t] from t_start to t_end

cos_end = cos(2 * pi * t_end / T)  # dimensionless

# Displacement during sliding: integral of velocity
# u = ∫[t_start to t_end] v(t) dt where v(t) = ∫[t_start to t] a_rel(tau) dtau
# u = ∫[t_start to t_end] ∫[t_start to t] (a_0*sin(2*pi*tau/T) - a_y) dtau dt

# = [-a_0*T^2/(4*pi^2)*sin(2*pi*t/T) - a_y*t^2/2 - C*t] from t_start to t_end
